body:
`case_study:svb-2023` | 2023-03-10 | tickers: US-SIVBQ | confidence: verified

SVB Financial peaked at ~$760 in Nov 2021 and failed on 10 Mar 2023 after customers tried to pull $42 bn on 9 Mar alone. Deposits had tripled 2019-21 with the VC boom (~$60 bn to ~$190 bn); SVB invested them in long-duration Treasuries/MBS, much of it classified held-to-maturity. At end-2022 unrealised HTM losses were ~$15 bn versus ~$16 bn of equity -- disclosed in the 10-K. ~90%+ of deposits were uninsured (NBER: 92.5%), concentrated in a networked VC/startup client base that was burning cash. 8 Mar: SVB announced a $1.8 bn loss on selling AFS securities and a $2.25 bn capital raise -> run. Visible flags: (1) HTM unrealised loss ~ equity (fair-value equity ~zero); (2) deposit base shrinking through 2022 as startups burned cash; (3) uninsured, concentrated deposits; (4) securities >50% of assets; no hedging of rate risk after removing swaps; (5) no chief risk officer for much of 2022; (6) CEO sold shares two weeks before failure under a pre-set plan. Lesson: for banks, mark the securities book to market and compare with equity; deposit concentration and uninsured share determine run speed. Social-media-era runs are hours, not weeks.

**Lesson:** Fair-value equity and deposit concentration decide bank survival
**Spotted early by:** some short sellers and analysts reading the 10-K HTM footnote
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:lender-blowup-signals`, illustrates -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
**Sources:** <https://www.icaew.com/insights/viewpoints-on-the-news/2023/mar-2023/chart-of-the-week-silicon-valley-bank> ; <https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w31048/revisions/w31048.rev0.pdf> ; <https://economics.yale.edu/sites/default/files/2024-02/metrick-2024-the-failure-of-silicon-valley-bank-and-the-panic-of-2023.pdf>

`insight:india-mb-how-they-end` · confidence: verified

Status on 19 Nov 2026 versus each stock's all-time high: 8 of 27 are ≥50% below (Symphony −74, KPIT −72, La Opala −66, Tata Elxsi −64, Alkyl −64, Kaynes −62, Cochin −60, Avanti −52); 5 more are 40–50% below (Deepak −50, Astral −48, Mazagon −47, Page −42, Trent −41); Suzlon is −56% from its 2024 turnaround peak. Still near highs (≤15% off): Eicher, Bajaj Finance, APL Apollo, Pidilite, Titan, BSE, HAL, BEL. Five ending mechanisms: (a) growth deceleration at a premium multiple (Page, Astral, Tata Elxsi, Trent, Symphony, La Opala, KPIT, Dixon); (b) commodity or spread reversal (Deepak, Alkyl, Avanti, Balkrishna's ROCE fall); (c) narrative timing slip (shipyards' P75(I) award); (d) earnings miss plus governance or disclosure question (Kaynes); (e) customer or regional concentration shock (KPIT on BMW and Europe, Tata Elxsi on JLR and autos, Avanti on US shrimp). The survivors share continuing double-digit EPS growth and a P/E that normalised gradually rather than being at a peak. Lesson: multibaggers are rentals more often than lifetime holdings. Define in advance the specific driver whose break means exit (LFL, spread, award, client), and track it quarterly.

body:
**Indian scuttlebutt checklist (questions that stay on generally available or observational ground):**
- *Dealers / distributors / retailers:* Which brand is gaining shelf space or counter share? Who gives the best margins and credit terms, and is that changing? Inventory days now versus 6 months ago? Do customers ask for the brand by name? Is the company pushing stock at quarter-end (channel stuffing)? How are payment terms enforced? Do they accept returns?
- *Customers (B2B):* Why did you choose them over the L1 bidder? Would you single-source? What is the switching cost? How is quality and delivery on time? Is your wallet share going up or down?
- *Suppliers:* Does the company pay on time? Are its order volumes rising? Has it asked for longer credit? (A strong early stress signal.)
- *Ex-employees (Glassdoor, LinkedIn, alumni):* Culture; how the promoter treats minority money; capex discipline; attrition in sales and R&D; **never** ask about unreleased numbers.
- *Competitors:* Who do you fear? Who is pricing irrationally? Who is losing people?
- *Physical checks:* plant visit (Is there an AGM plant tour? Is the plant running shifts? Truck queues?), job postings for the new plant, the new plant on satellite imagery (Google Earth timeline), app-store reviews, quick-commerce and e-commerce rank, a mystery-shopper visit to a showroom.
- *Records:* MCA charges register (new borrowings), court cases (eCourts), the factory licence, pollution-board consent-to-operate for the new capacity (state PCB sites list CTO/CTE approvals, which confirm capex timelines independently of management).

`person:group-tvs` · flag: **mostly-clean** · confidence: verified · tickers: TVSMOTOR, TVSHLTD, SUNDARMFIN, TVSSCS, SUNCLAY

Flag: MOSTLY-CLEAN. The wider TVS family divided the group in 2020 (TVS Motor, Sundaram-Clayton and holdco TVS Holdings to Venu Srinivasan's branch; Sundaram Finance, Lucas-TVS, Sundram Fasteners etc. to other branches) -- an orderly partition with no listed-company value transfer reported. TVS Motor has been a strong compounder with low promoter pledging and steady dividends; Sundaram Finance is a conservative lender with a long clean record. Capital allocation debates: TVS Motor's overseas bets (Norton, Swiss e-bike brands) and Sundaram-Clayton/TVS Holdings restructuring that created a holdco layer. New 2026 risk: an open ownership dispute inside Venu Srinivasan's family. Venu and son Sudarshan Venu say a March-2024 MoU split the businesses; wife Mallika Srinivasan (TAFE chair) and daughter Lakshmi Venu said on 13-Oct-2026 that 'no economic settlement has been reached', and Lakshmi sent a partition notice. TVS Holdings disclosed Sudarshan as a significant beneficial owner via trust structures; the VS Trust holds 66.55% of TVS Holdings. No regulator findings of wrongdoing. Investor read: governance of operating companies is good; the dispute is a control/succession overhang at the holdco level that could affect board stability or force stake monetisation.

- **red flags:** 2026 father-daughter ownership dispute; holdco layering
- **good conduct:** orderly 2020 partition; no pledges
